clue.text: Hear some rubbish about quiet signalling system

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters sit around the letter for quiet
rubbish suggests the words hear and some are junk to be thrown together into a new order

parts.note: P (piano) is the musical abbreviation for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone is told to listen to some nonsense concerning a silent method of sending messages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rubbish' reorders HEARSOME into SEMAHORE, and 'about' wraps that round P so it lands between A and H.
explanation.definitionFit: Semaphore is a method of sending messages with flags or mechanical arms held in coded positions.

clue.text: Confound the newspaper leader backing the row!

indicators.note: backing means the abbreviation for the newspaper's chief is set down back to front

parts.note: the editor, abbreviated ED, is the person leading a newspaper
a range is a row or line, as of mountains

explanation.surface: An exclamation of frustration at the editor of a paper supporting a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns ED into DE; 'row' looks like a quarrel but is a line, RANGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To derange is to throw into confusion or disorder, which is what confounding does.

clue.text: Given no details of the situation, so shut up at this point

definitions.text: Given no details of the situation

parts.note: taken as written
to mew is to confine or shut up, as hawks were kept in a mews
here means at this point or place

explanation.surface: Someone vague about a location tells another to be quiet right now.
explanation.walkthrough: MEW in the sense of confining (a hawk in its mews) is an old word solvers may not know.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying a thing is in an unspecified place means its location is given without detail.

clue.text: Gather together sheep, and fleece

parts.note: stock is farm livestock, such as a flock of sheep
pile is the soft raised nap of a fleece or fabric

explanation.surface: A shepherd rounds up the flock and shears their wool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fleece' reads as a verb meaning rob, but it is the noun, the woolly nap called PILE.
explanation.definitionFit: To stockpile is to accumulate supplies and hoard them for later use.

clue.text: Roman philosopher creating a scene

indicators.note: creating suggests the words a scene are worked into something new by reordering

explanation.surface: An ancient thinker making a fuss in public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'creating a scene' reads as making a fuss; 'creating' reorders the letters of A SCENE.
explanation.definitionFit: Seneca the Younger was a Stoic thinker and tutor to the emperor Nero.

clue.text: Neat accommodation

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so this is lodging for cows rather than tidy rooms

explanation.surface: Tidy lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: NEAT is an archaic word for cattle, as in neat's-foot oil; the clue pretends to describe tidy rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A shed or byre where cattle are housed is lodging for neat, an old word for oxen.

clue.text: This Shakespearean character having money, tried a questionable set-up

parts.note: P stands for penny, a unit of money

indicators.note: a questionable set-up is a dubious arrangement, so the letters of tried a are rearranged

explanation.surface: A figure from Shakespeare who, being wealthy, attempted a dodgy arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'questionable set-up' rearranges TRIEDA into ERDITA; the linked 7-down borrows this clue's definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Perdita is the lost princess of The Winter's Tale, a Shakespeare play.

clue.text: … but this one backed genuine set-up

indicators.note: backed means the word for genuine is written back to front

parts.note: real means genuine

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word set is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue, another character supported an authentic arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from 6-down, so 'this one' means another Shakespearean character. 'backed' turns REAL into LAER and 'up' turns SET into TES.
explanation.definitionFit: Laertes is Ophelia's brother in Hamlet, another figure from Shakespeare's plays.

clue.text: Overlooks cash spent abroad a bad thing indeed

parts.note: eyes, as a verb, means looks over or regards
an ore is a small coin of Sweden, Denmark and Norway

explanation.surface: Someone ignores money squandered on a foreign trip, which is truly terrible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overlooks' suggests ignoring, but here it means looks over, EYES. ORE is a Scandinavian coin.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyesore is something ugly to look at, a blot on the landscape.

clue.text: Being small, got heated when crowded

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
warmed means got heated

explanation.surface: Being little, someone grew hot in a packed room.
explanation.definitionFit: Swarmed means thronged or packed together in large numbers, as a crowd does.

clue.text: College, one admitting almost a half

indicators.note: admitting means the word for one lets the other letters in

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards or dice

indicators.note: almost means the word for half loses its final letter

parts.note: demi is a prefix meaning half

explanation.surface: A college takes in a student who is nearly half-way through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims DEMI to DEM. ACE is a one at cards or dice.
explanation.definitionFit: Academe is the academic world of universities and colleges.

clue.text: Cessation may be arranged by sporting individuals

indicators.note: may be arranged tells the solver the letters of cessation can be put in a different order

explanation.surface: An end to hostilities could be organised by athletes.
explanation.definitionFit: Canoeists are people who paddle canoes for sport.

clue.text: Get on — as the result of a loan?

definitions.meaning: to get on is to go forward or make progress
money paid out before it is due, a sum lent

explanation.definitionFit: To advance is to move forward, and an advance is a sum lent or paid early.

clue.text: Large measure of drink for swinish boss?

definitions.meaning: a large cask holding about fifty gallons of wine or beer
the chief of a pig, read as the pig's own top part

explanation.definitionFit: A hogshead is a large barrel, and a pig's head is jokingly its boss.

clue.text: Nautical gear, note, is quite thin

parts.note: spars are the masts, booms and yards of a ship
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A sailor's rigging and a musical tone are rather meagre.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparse means thinly scattered or scanty.

clue.text: Suggesting. professional modelling

parts.note: pro is short for professional
posing is what a model does for an artist or photographer

explanation.surface: A hint that someone is a paid model.
explanation.definitionFit: Proposing means putting forward an idea for consideration.

clue.text: Oriental guys, far from modish, being set right

parts.note: E stands for east, the Orient
men means guys
dated means old-fashioned, far from fashionable

explanation.surface: Eastern men, very unfashionable, are being corrected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' only joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Emendated means corrected, as a scholar corrects a text.

clue.text: One way or another, do some decorating again

indicators.note: one way or another says the word reads the same whichever direction it is taken

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Somehow or other, someone redecorates the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One way or another' reads as a shrug in the surface, but it says the entry reads identically forwards and backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To repaper a room is to hang fresh wallpaper on its walls once more.

clue.text: Does time for mistreating old people

indicators.note: mistreating means the words does time are handled roughly and reordered

explanation.surface: Serving a prison sentence for abusing the elderly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old people' reads as pensioners, but means an ancient nation; 'for' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: The Edomites were an ancient Semitic nation descended, in the Bible, from Esau.

clue.text: Produced designs and so on a man would follow

indicators.note: follow means the letters for a man would come after the abbreviation

parts.note: etc is short for et cetera, and so on
he'd is the contraction of he would

explanation.surface: A man would come after, producing patterns and the like.
explanation.definitionFit: Etched means cut designs into metal or glass with acid or a point.

clue.text: A judge without honour — smarter, though!

indicators.note: without, in its old sense of outside, means the word for judge goes round the honour

parts.note: a trier is one who tries a case, a judge
MM, the Military Medal, is an honour

explanation.surface: A judge lacking integrity is nonetheless better dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking. MM is the Military Medal, a British award for bravery.
explanation.definitionFit: Trimmer means neater and more smartly turned out.

clue.text: Races held by those involved to be most exciting

indicators.note: held by means the races are kept inside the jumbled letters
involved means the letters of those are tangled into a new order

parts.note: TT, the Tourist Trophy, is the motorcycle races on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Contests run by the participants are thrilling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges THOSE into HOEST. TT races are the Isle of Man motorcycle races.
explanation.definitionFit: Hottest in the sense of most thrilling or most sensational.

clue.text: Little beasts pocketing loot can give rise to complaint

indicators.note: pocketing means the small animals take the word for loot inside

parts.note: mice are little animals
to rob is to loot

explanation.surface: Small creatures stealing food could provoke grievances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' looks like a grievance but means an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A germ may cause disease, and complaint is an old word for an ailment.

clue.text: Organising a camping expedition

indicators.note: organising suggests the letters of a camping are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone plans a trip to camp out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expedition' reads as a camping trip, but is a military operation.
explanation.definitionFit: A campaign is a series of military operations, a planned expedition of war.

clue.text: A bowed old soldier

parts.note: reads as a stooping veteran, but means a soldier of old armed with a bow

explanation.surface: A stooped veteran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowed' suggests stooping with age; it means carrying a bow.
explanation.definitionFit: Bowmen fought in medieval armies, shooting arrows with longbows.

clue.text: Sort of paint responsible for illness

definitions.meaning: a water-based paint for walls, used by artists and decorators
a viral disease of dogs and other animals

explanation.definitionFit: Distemper is both a glue-bound wall paint and a contagious canine disease.

clue.text: Italian place accountants rate, unsound

parts.note: CAs are chartered accountants

indicators.note: unsound means the word rate is broken and rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: Bookkeepers judge an Italian town to be unreliable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsound' rearranges RATE into ERTA. CA is a chartered accountant.
explanation.definitionFit: Caserta is a city near Naples, famous for its royal palace.

clue.text: A woman keeping a snug home is forgiving

indicators.note: keeping means the woman's name holds the home inside it

parts.note: Amy is a woman's name
a nest is a cosy home

explanation.surface: A woman with a cosy house is a merciful person.
explanation.definitionFit: An amnesty is a general pardon, an act of official forgiving.

clue.text: Honour within reason when no blemishes are apparent

indicators.note: within means the letters sit inside the words when no blemishes

explanation.surface: Praise is reasonable when there are no faults to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within reason' looks like a phrase meaning moderately, but 'within' signals the letters in WHEN NO BLEMISHES.
explanation.definitionFit: To ennoble is to raise someone to the nobility, honouring them.

clue.text: The person agitating for an investigator

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a tester is one who examines or investigates

explanation.surface: An activist is in favour of an inquirer.
explanation.definitionFit: A protester campaigns for or against a cause, stirring up opinion.
